Q01.note: All seven ground truthful certification and crew safety in the same places: each strand's own exposition of the truth and neighbor-protection commandments (LC 8th/7th/5th, WLC 144-145, catechism duty, General Rules, Schleitheim truthful speech) plus the same Scripture (Exod 20:16, Eph 4:25, Prov 12:22).

Q02.note: The Reformed column grounds refusal in the WCF's binding Sabbath rest (career advancement neither necessity nor mercy) while the Lutheran column cites AC XXVIII against any new-sabbath law and the Pentecostal column certifies as an absence that no standard forbids Sunday work (Anabaptist likewise has no sabbath article) — contradictory doctrinal claims about the Lord's Day.

Q03.note: Matt 18:15 private-first and Rom 12:19-21 no-revenge carry every column, with each strand's own exposition (LC 8th, WLC 144-145, Wesley's Cure of Evil-Speaking, Dordrecht defenselessness) making the same claims.

Q04.note: Prov 31:8-9 plus each strand's doctrinally equivalent duty-to-defend / sin-of-omission locus (LC 8th and 5th, WLC 145's 'undue silence', the General Confession's things-left-undone, BF&M XV, General Rules) do identical work.

Q05.note: A shared 1 Cor 7:17/Col 3:23 core, but the weight sits on different strand-specific vocation loci — AC XVI/XXVII, WSC Q1, the catechism's state-of-life duty, Wesley's Use of Money, CFMP creation-and-calling — all dignifying ordinary work against a sacred/secular ladder.

Q06.note: Matt 18:15, Eph 4:28, and restitution taught by each strand's equivalent locus (LC 7th, WLC 141, the Communion exhortation's restitution, Luke 19:8) make the same confess-restore-privately-first claims.

Q07.note: Mark 8:36 with each strand's First-Commandment/idolatry exposition (LC 1st, WLC 105, treasures-on-earth, Luke 12's barns) and the same parental texts (Eph 6:4, Deut 6:6-7) do the same work everywhere.

Q08.note: The Pentecostal column grounds giving in Mal 3:8-10 tithing as the scriptural standard (an expected covenant practice in CoG/COGIC) while the Lutheran (AC XXVIII/Apology: human rules cannot bind consciences), Reformed (WCF liberty of conscience, no fixed percentage), Anglican, and Anabaptist columns assert their standards bind no tenth — a contradiction over whether the tithe binds.

Q09.note: The same stop-and-disclose claim is carried by different strand-specific instruments — WLC 142's named 'wasteful gaming', SBC anti-gambling resolutions, UMC Social Principles and the Nazarene covenant, the AG gambling paper — while Lutheran, Anglican, and Anabaptist columns reach it by commandment extension.

Q10.note: Eph 4:25, Prov 28:13, and the one-flesh/marriage loci (LC 8th, WLC 144-145 with WCF repentance-to-the-party-offended, marriage rite, BF&M XVIII, CFMP truth-telling) ground the same disclose-with-repentance claim in every column.

Q11.note: Proverbs' suretyship warnings (22:26-27; 17:18; 6:1-5) are the named primary carrier in all seven columns — several noting their confessions do not treat surety — with stewardship and honor-of-parents loci secondary and agreeing.

Q12.note: 1 Cor 6:1-7 and the Matt 5 / Luke 12 peace texts ground every column's same claim (avoid litigation with kin, prefer peace, keep-or-split left free); the Lutheran lawful-courts accent and Anabaptist nonresistance accent both still permit honest defense and prefer mediation on these facts.

Q13.note: Rom 13:1-7 / Matt 22:21 with James 5:4 and each strand's civil-obedience and honest-gain loci (Table of Duties, WLC 142, obedience homily, BF&M XVII, General Rules' unpaid-duty example, Dordrecht 13) make the same render-what-is-owed claim.

Q14.note: Matt 5:42 and Prov 19:17 plus each strand's equivalent mercy locus (LC 5th, WLC 141, Article XXXVIII with the alms homily, General Rules, CFMP mutual aid) command the same open-handed mercy with the form left free.

Q15.note: Matt 19:6 / Mark 10 with Mal 2 and each strand's lifelong-covenant locus (WCF marriage chapter, the marriage rite's mutual society, BF&M XVIII, Social Principles/Nazarene covenant, CFMP 19) make the same repair-not-exit claim with the same abuse caveat.

Q16.note: Matt 5:27-28 and Job 31:1 carry every column, with each strand's purity standard (WLC 139's named 'lascivious pictures', the whoredom homily, BF&M XV naming pornography, Social Principles/Nazarene, CoG moral purity) making the same adultery-of-the-heart claim against 'it is not cheating'.

Q17.note: Every column grounds the wronged spouse's freedom in Matt 19:9 with 1 Cor 7:15 and 7:39, the WCF stating the same innocent-party claim confessionally; stricter wings (historic CoG/COGIC, Old Order) appear only as internal variation, not as any column's grounding claim.

Q18.note: Luke 15 and Luke 5:29-32 with 1 Cor 5:9-11's inside/outside-the-church distinction ground the same chastity-affirmed, presence-with-witness claim in all six speaking columns (Pentecostal silent).

Q19.note: 2 Cor 6:14 and 1 Cor 7:39 'only in the Lord' carry all seven columns, with WCF, the 1689, and Dordrecht 12 stating the identical rule and all distinguishing 1 Cor 7:12-14 as about remaining, not entering.

Q20.note: Eph 6:4's two ditches (provoke not / bring them up) plus each strand's nurture locus (Table of Duties, WLC 129, baptismal charge, BF&M XVIII, Wesley's family-religion sermons, CFMP 19) ground the same relationship-plus-order claim.

Q21.note: 1 Tim 5:4,8, Mark 7:9-13's Corban rebuke, and Exod 20:12 honor expositions carry all seven columns; every strand's claim is the same — the care binds, the housing form is wisdom.

Q22.note: Only Baptist and Pentecostal speak (five strands silent), both grounding in Ps 139:13-16 and 1 Samuel 1 plus their bodies' equivalent sanctity-of-life-from-conception statements making the same embryo-protection cautions without forbidding IVF.

Q23.note: Gen 2:24 leave-and-cleave with Col 3:19,21 / Eph 6:4 and each strand's household-duty locus (Table of Duties, WLC 129-130, marriage rite and matrimony homily, BF&M XVIII, Wesley's On Family Religion) ground the same the-husband-must-act claim (Pentecostal silent).

Q24.note: The Baptist column's BF&M 2000 grounds the wife's gracious submission to the husband's servant leadership while the Methodist column's standards reject one gender's dominance and expressly decline to import the husband-decides framework — with the Anglican 'obey' vow and Pentecostal wings split the same way — contradictory doctrinal claims about marital decision authority, the case's exact question.

Q25.note: The same medicine-is-not-unbelief work is done by different strand-specific loci — First-Article providence through creatures, WLC 135's 'sober use of physic', the Visitation of the Sick, the SBC mental-health resolution, the Nazarene Divine Healing article's medical clause, and AG position papers against faith-metering.

Q26.note: Pentecostal (AG/CoG/COGIC) and Nazarene standards — and the Baptist covenant clause — ground total abstinence as the standard, while the Lutheran, Reformed, and Anglican columns assert wine is God's gift, moderation the rule, and abstinence not imposable on conscience as law: contradictory claims about whether drink itself is forbidden.

Q27.note: The Pentecostal column grounds counsel in divine healing provided for all in the atonement while the Reformed and Anglican columns ground the same pain in providence's fatherly hand and God's visitation for the trial of patience (and the Lutheran in anti-enthusiasm) — different doctrinal claims about what her sickness is and what deliverance is provided, though all reject the friend's faith-meter.

Q28.note: Matt 6:16-18, Col 2:23, and 1 Cor 6:19-20 with each strand's fasting-as-means-not-end locus (AC XXVI, WCF's occasional fasts and good-works chapters, the fasting homily, General Rules' ordinance list, CFMP 18) make the same claim in all six speaking columns (Pentecostal silent).

Q29.note: Prov 28:13, 1 John 1:9, and Jas 5:16 carry every column, with each strand's restoration-after-fall article (AC XII, Article XVI, Dort Fifth Head, Of Sin After Justification) making the same the-fall-is-not-final, disclose-and-return claim.

Q30.note: Phil 4:6-7 read as invitation-with-promise (never accusation) carries all seven columns, with each strand's means/medicine locus (law-gospel distinction, WLC 135, Visitation office, SBC resolution, Heaviness sermon, AG papers, CFMP providence) making the same no-condemnation-plus-treatment claim.

Q31.note: Phil 1:21-23 / 2 Tim 4:6-8 resurrection hope plus each strand's own statement that declining burdensome treatment is not hastening death (WLC 136's means-language, Visitation/Burial offices, BF&M XV natural death, Social Principles, AG end-of-life position) ground the same distinction in all six speaking columns (Anabaptist silent).

Q32.note: Gen 1:27 and Jas 3:9-10 carry every column, with each strand's racism-named-as-sin instrument (BF&M XV, 1995 SBC resolution, Social Principles, Memphis 1994, Belhar where adopted) and the Matt 18 private word making the same claims.

Q33.note: The same keep-the-friend, conscience-unbound work is done by different strand loci — AC XVI's penultimate civic order, WCF liberty of conscience, the strife-and-charity homilies, Wesley's Catholic Spirit and anti-bigotry sermons, CFMP heavenly citizenship — with only thin shared Scripture (Baptist and Pentecostal silent).

Q34.note: Heb 10:24-25, Acts 2:42-46, and Gen 2:18 carry all six speaking columns, with equivalent communion-of-saints/church loci (WCF, Belgic 28, BF&M VI covenant, Wesley's social-religion sermon and class system, AG Church article, CFMP 9) making the same belonging-by-covenant claim (Anglican silent).

Q35.note: Each strand's Eighth/Ninth-Commandment tongue exposition (LC, WLC 144-145's talebearing and receiving evil reports, catechism, the covenant's tattling clause, Cure of Evil-Speaking) and the same Proverbs 26 / James 4:11 texts make the identical leave-defend-and-help claim.

Q36.note: Ex 20:14,16, Eph 5:11, and Gal 6:1 ground the same no-lie-no-complicity-restore-gently claim in every column; the Anabaptist oath articles (Schleitheim 7, Dordrecht 15) are doing the identical truth-telling work here, not a contested claim.

Q37.note: AC XVI, the WCF, Article XXXVII, and the 1689 assert Christians may lawfully bear arms in just wars while Schleitheim 6, Dordrecht 14, and CFMP 22 assert the sword lies outside the perfection of Christ and forbid participation in war — with Methodist standards internally holding war contrary to Christ's spirit — head-on contradictory claims on the case's question.

Q38.note: The lawful-oath articles (AC XVI, the WCF chapter under which refusing a lawfully imposed oath is sin, Article XXXIX, the 1689, the Methodist article) directly contradict Schleitheim 7 / Dordrecht 15 / James 5:12 forbidding all swearing, the two sides reading Matt 5:33-37 in opposite ways (Pentecostal silent).

Q39.note: AC XVI and Article XXXVII assert Christians may lawfully sit in judgment and award punishment (even death) while Schleitheim 6 asserts Christ's followers do not pass such sentence — Old Order counsel is to seek excusal — contradictory claims about whether the verdict is his to render (Pentecostal silent).

Q40.note: The three speaking columns (four strands silent) do the same conscience-free, no-contempt work through different loci — BF&M XVII religious liberty, Social Principles' commended participation, Schleitheim-shaped reserve with Phil 3:20 — their leans toward voting or abstention differing without contradictory claims, since each column leaves both free.

Q41.note: Luke 10:25-37, Lev 19:33-34, and Matt 25:35-40 carry all seven columns' identical claims: mercy to the persons is commanded regardless of status, enforcement belongs to the magistrate, and no deception of authority is counseled.

Q42.note: The two speaking columns (five strands silent) ground the same consolation-is-mutual-and-embodied claim in Gen 2:18 and Jas 5:16 plus equivalent loci — the Smalcald mutual consolation of the brethren and BF&M VI's doctrine of the church with the ERLC/SBC AI statements.

Q43.note: Eph 4:26-27 and Phil 4:8 with each strand's anger exposition (LC 5th/8th, WLC 99 with 136, the Litany and contention homily, the covenant's anger clause, General Rules' diversions-and-reading examples) make the same starve-the-wrath claim in all six speaking columns (Pentecostal silent).

Q44.note: 1 Thess 4:13 grief-with-hope and each strand's mourning-carried-in-the-body locus (communion of saints, Burial office, church covenant, General Rules watching-over, mourning beatitude, CFMP 9) make the same claim in all six speaking columns (Pentecostal silent).

Q45.note: The same return-to-the-appointed-means-and-keep-asking work is done by different strand machinery — command-promise-need with fixed forms, HC 116 with the WCF's intermitted assurance, the daily office, Wesley's Means of Grace and Wilderness State, sought Spirit-enabled prayer, communal practice — the Pentecostal Spirit-baptism accent being a strand-specific means, not a claim any other column contests here.

Q46.note: The Reformed column asserts the former ways of revealing have ceased and nothing is added by new revelations, and the Lutheran that God does not deal through unmediated inner voices, while the Pentecostal column honors promptings and congregationally judged prophetic words as real, testable leading — contradictory claims about whether his impression could be God speaking.

Q47.note: The Reformed and Baptist columns ground his comfort in perseverance (Dort: God surely renews his own; BF&M V: kept and persevering to the end) while the Pentecostal grounds it in conditional security (a believer can genuinely fall away and be restored) and the Methodist in recoverable departure from grace — contradictory security doctrines carrying the same welcome home.

Q48.note: The Methodist column grounds hope in entire sanctification — grace can purify the heart's bent, not merely restrain it — while the Reformed column's Heidelberg locus asserts even the holiest attain only a small beginning of this obedience in this life: different doctrinal claims about the attainable cure of his envy, though the practices counseled coincide.

Q49.note: Ps 139:13-16, 2 Sam 12:23, and 1 Thess 4:13 carry all six speaking columns (Anglican silent), with the infant-salvation comfort aligned in claim across its forms — Dort I.17 confessionally, Baptist consensus conviction, Lutheran commendation to God's mercy without any rite-dependence.

Q50.note: Vacuous code: all seven worksheets declare silence (their standards do not address burial versus cremation), so there are no non-silent groundings to compare; recorded as shared by convention with this note rather than left absent.
